title: CBP deploys to support Hurricane Florence relief
description: CBP Air and Marine Operations brings CBP communications personnel and equipment to Manassas Va airport to stage in preparation to move into the Carolinas to support federal state and local rescue and law enforcement partners during hurricane operations
unit_name: U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office of Public Affairs - Visual Communications Division

transcript.text: This morning we flew from the Hammond Airport home of the New Orleans Air Marine branch.
We brought part of the GTAC team, the ground air coordinating team.
They're going to be providing services, primarily dealing with communications.
And we decided to go ahead and deploy early to have everything in place.
So when the need arose, we'd be ready to go.
Well, we got to call this morning and here we are four hours later.
We move from generally the New Orleans area and here we are near Washington DC.
And I'm sure this will be the first of many runs that we're going to be doing over the next
however long it takes. It doesn't take long. We're a very streamlined organization.
We get the job done. When the phone call comes in, we go through the paperwork,
we operate safely and efficiently. We're ready to go.
We have to make sure that we have backup towers. We have mobile towers that we can use.
Communications is always key. We've got to be able to talk to each other.
So they're trying to anticipate whatever those needs may be so they can respond with our IT folks
and make sure that the communications network stays in TAC no matter what. It's a key part of this.
One of the really unique things we can do at CBP is support our state and local law enforcement
agencies. They may not have the assets and personnel and the technology that we have on our side of
the house. So we'll work with the county and the state officials to make sure that we integrate with
them. The unique thing about the state and local partners that we work with, they know the local
area. They'll know where the communications towers are. They'll know where the hospitals are. They'll
know where all these facilities are. So what we'll be able to do is have in advance all that information
so that when the storm does move and when there as soon as the needs arise, we'll be able to respond
again very efficiently with them partnering with our state and local agencies.
